caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No.8 of 1979.
lawyer:
MihirKanti Majumder with Hemayet Hossain, Jatirmoya Deb for Jitendra Narayan Deb, Advocates ----- For the Appellants,
BK Das, Advocate ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Madaris Ali and others ----- Appellants
Vs
Biswamber Das Being dead his heirs ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque, J.: This appeal at the instance of the principal defendant defendant Nos. 1 to 13 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30th November, 1977 passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Additional Court, Sylhet, in Title Suit No. 43 of 1977 decreeing plaintiffs suit for declaration of title in the suit land.

2. Case of the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1 to 36, in short, is as follows:

The suit land masuring 26.22 acres originally belonged to Syedunnessa Chowdurani and Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and their co-sharers, predecessors of the proforma defendant Nos. 14 to 21. The said land was lying vacant and is situated far away from the houses of the landlords. The plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from the landlords 49 years ago at an annual rental at the rate of half a maund of paddy per kedar. The plaintiffs, thereafter, reclaimed the suit land and grew paddy and they paid rent to the Zamindars through the Morals and some of the landlords received sale proceeds after selling paddy rent collected by the Morals, Share of the plaintiffs in the suit land is equal and subsequently for convenience of possession they got the same partitioned by 'Ails' but continued to pay paddy rent together.

3. Further case of the plaintiffs is that they being illiterate simple village folk they entrusted Morals and employees of the Zamindars with recording of their names during the settlement operation and they believed that their names were correctly recorded in the settlement papers. Principal defendants disclosed on 1st/2nd Chaitra, 1381 BS that they purchased the suit land from the proforma defendants and asked the plaintiffs to make over possession of the same to them. Plaintiffs doubted their claim and enquired into the Tahsil Office and came to learn that the employees of the landlords in collusion with the settlement staff got the suit land recorded as Khas Dakhuli land of the landlords. Proforma defendants never claimed the suit land on the basis of the wrong records nor did the same affect their title. Principal defendants obtained void, fraudulent, collusive sale deed from some of the greedy proforma defendants after coming to learn about the recording of the suit land in their names and thus clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The plaintiffs on the basis of their settlement and adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation to the knowledge of all acquired title in the suit land and, as such, they are entitled to get their title declared.

4. Defendant Nos. 1 to 8, 10 and 13 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. Proforma defendant Nos. 14 to 19 also filed a joint written statement but they ultimately did not contest the suit.

5. Contesting defendant Nos. 1 to 8, 10 and 13 denied the material allegations made in the plaint. They further averred that the plaintiffs suit is not maintainable and barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Their specific case is that Syedunnessa Chowdhurani, Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others did never settle the suit land 40 years ago or at any time with the plaintiffs at an annual rental of half a maund of paddy per kedar or any rent nor they realised any rent from them. Suit land was Khas dakhali land of the said landlords and the same was fallow land even during the land settlement operation and recorded as such in the name of the proforma defendants in the khatians. In 1380 BS principal defendants entered into an agreement with the proforma defendants to purchase the suit land at the rate of Tk. 1250.00 per acre and with the permission of the said owners principal defendant Nos. 14 to 19 sold 24 acre of the suit land in their 14 annas 12 gondas 35 tils share at a consideration of Tk. 30,000 to the principal defendants by a registered sale deed dated 22nd Falgoon, 1381 BS (27.3.75) and the said sellers relinquished all their right, title and interest in the said land in favour of defendants 1 to 13 and the principal defendants have been possessing the same along with 1 anna 7 gondas 3 koras 5 tils shares of proforma defendants 20 and 21 who could not execute and register the sale deed for some difficulties but made over possession of the same to the defendants 1 to 13. Plaintiffs failed to purchase the suit land as the principal defendants offered more money than they had offered and they filed the suit on false allegation of settlement. They had never any title and possession in the suit land.

6. Plaintiffs examined 6 witnesses including plaintiff No. 3 Mobarak Ali as PW 1 and also produced and proved some Toka Farags Exts. 1 to 1 (r) in support of their case. Contesting defendants examined 5 witnesses including defendant No. 7 Rowab Ali as DW 1 and also produced and proved some documents such as finally published Khatians Ext. A (2), the government rent receipts Ext. B to B(2) and certified copy of their kabala Ext. C.

7. Oil consideration of the said evidence court below decreed the suit after arriving at the following conclusion:

"In spite of all the defects in" the Toka farags it has now become clear that the plaintiffs have their legs on the suit land and whatever defects crept in the Toka farags have since been perfected by the long user of the suit land by the plaintiffs beyond the statutory period of limitation to the knowledge of the original owners. Khatian Ext A is found to be erroneous and kabala Ext. C is found to have no legal effect. As the plaintiffs have clear title and possession in the suit land the suit is found to be maintainable in the present form."

8. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder along with Mr. Hemayet Hossain and Mr. Jotirmoya Deb. learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of Mr. Jitendra Narayan Deb for the appellants, placed before us plaint, written statement, deposition of the witnesses, impugned judgment and other materials on record. The learned Advocate submitted that the plaintiffs failed to establish their alleged claim of settlement of the suit land on the basis of Toka farags Ext. 1 series which are neither in the name of any of the plaintiffs nor any particulars of the suit land mentioned therein. He further submitted that the plaintiffs also failed to establish their alleged adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. He further submitted that the suit land was recorded in the name of predecessor-in-interest of the proforma defendants in finally published Khatians after factual field survey in the locality and the suit land has been recorded as fallow land (layek-patiti/ Layek ura).

9. Mr. BK Das, learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, strenuously argued that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land for the last 40 years beyond the statutory period of limitation and thereby acquired title in the suit land by adverse possession, even if they failed to establish their settlement of the same from the landlords. He further submitted that the kabala Ext. C of the principal defendants shows that the suit land is cultivable land and not fallow land at the time of their purchase and defendants' story that the suit land was fallow Khas land of the landlords is belied by such recital in their sale deed.

10. In this case admittedly the suit land belonged to the predecessors-in-interest of the proforma defendants and it was their vacant Khas land and finally published khatians Ext. A series recorded the same in the name of the said landlords as their Khas land. The question in whether the said landlords settled the same with the plaintiffs and or the plaintiffs acquired title therein by adverse possession.

11. PW 1 in his deposition stated that the suit land was lying fallow, situated far away from the house of the landlords and near their house and they took settlement of the same about 40 year before and they reclaimed the same and made it fit for seedling bed. No other witness supported the PW 1 in this respect. There is no particular as regards date, time, place and persons from whom and in whose presence plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land. There is also no document in support of such settlement of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs. Of course, the plaintiffs have produced some Toka farags or receipts Ext.1 series but none of those Toka farags are in the name of any of the plaintiffs nor there is any particular of the land in respect of which rent was realized by the said Toka farags PW 6 Dinash Chandra Chakrabarty who claimed to have served in the Sheristha of the said landlords from 1329 BS to 1349/1350 BS formally proved Toka farags dated 21.2.55 BS Ext. 1(L), 4.9.59 BS Ext. 1(10), 12.8.59 BS Ext. 1(q) and 2.3.59 BS Ext 1(r) to be in the handwriting of Abdus Shahid, another employee of the Zamindars. He also proved Toka farag dated 7.3.62 BS Ext. 1(n) to be in the handwriting of Naresh another employee of the said Zamindars and also Toka farag dated 7.5.61. BS Ext. 1(k) to be in the handwriting of Surendra, another employee of the said Zamindars. He did not say that the said Toka farags were granted in his presence. He admitted in cross-examination that the landlords had a big sheristha and had printed farags and dakhilas and other registers. As we have already noticed that the said Toka farags are neither in the name of any of the plaintiffs nor in respect of the suit land. Merely because the said Zamindars are not coming to dispute the claim of the plaintiff it could not be said that the plaintiffs got settlement of the suit land on the basis of the said Toka farags. We, therefore, hold that the plaintiffs failed to prove that they took settlement of the suit land from the then landlords predecessors-in-interest of the proforma defendant Nos. 14 to 21 about 40 years ago or at any time.

12. Plaintiffs claimed title in the suit land on the basis of their settlement as well as adverse possession. As the plaintiffs failed to prove their settlement of the suit lands now let us see whether they have been able to prove their possession beyond the statutory period of limitation adversely to the true owners.

13. There is no case of the plaintiffs that they entered into the suit lands forcibly at any point of time to the knowledge of the said landlords, who admittedly reside far away and who has no tahsil office in the locality, denying title of the said landlords. Admittedly suit land was recorded in the name of the landlords Sayedunnessa Chowdhurani and Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others in Khatian Nos. 16 and 112 of mouza Purnakhola and Khatian No. 581 of Mouza Chaluia Exts. A-(2) and the said land has been recorded as fallow land in khas possessions of the said persons. It is admitted by the learned Advocates of both the parties that at the time of acquisition of rent receiving interest under the SAT Act field survey operation for preparation of record of rights under the provisions of Sylhet Tenancy Act 1936 in the suit locality was going on and ultimately the record of rights were prepared and finally published under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as there was no previous settlement operation in the District of Sylhet. Relying on the evidence of PW 1 the learned Advocate for the respondents contended that the said Khatians were wrongly prepared in the name of the landlords. PW 1 in his deposition stated that during last settlement operation they entrusted Morals and Karmacharies of landlords to record the suit land in their name. But in cross-examination he admitted that he has other lands besides the suit land and those were correctly recorded in his name. We have already seen that there was no tahsil office of the Zamindars in the locality and as such entrusting Karmacharies of the Zamindars cannot be relied on. None has corroborated the PW 1 in this respect and he also failed to name the Moral or Karmachari whom the plaintiffs had entrusted for the purpose. Moreover, the plaintiffs never took care to enquire about the Khatians within the period of 12 years from the date of final publication of the Khatians in 1963 and they only enquired about the Khatians in 1975 when they came to know from the principal defendants about the sale of the suit land by the proforma defendants to the principal defendants. The plaintiffs neither claimed to have paid any rent to the Government from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit in 1382 BS nor produced and proved any rent receipts. In view of the above it is difficult to hold that the said Khatians were not correctly prepared in the name of said Zamindars. Such finally published SA Khatians prepared after field survey operation stand on much better footing and more reliable than the SA Khatians made by merely revising the CS Khatians.

14. Now coming to the evidence of possession it is seen that PW 1 simply said that they reclaimed the suit land and made it fit for seedling bed, whereas the plaint case is that they grew paddy in the suit land after reclaiming the same. He even failed to give number and area of the suit land and area under possession of other plaintiffs or quantity of paddy delivered as rent. Though he said that Majid Moral now deceased realized paddy but admitted that he did not grant receipt of paddy. PW 2 simply said that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land for about 40 years. PW 3 stated that he has been seeing the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land since dawn of his knowledge. PW 5 stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. But none of those witnesses stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by growing paddy or as seedling bed. Only PW 4 who is a relation of plaintiff No. 11 Asmat Ali stated that the suit land Laye kpatit formerly and yield boro paddy and the plaintiffs have been possessing the same. PW 2 claimed himself to be 80 years old but in cross-examination he said that he had been seeing possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land since his boyhood which is contrary to the plaint case. He is resident of a different village Daudpur and his homestead is half a mile away from the suit land. He has no land near the suit land. PW 3 is an old man of 65 years. In cross-examination he has stated that knowledge dawned in him at the age of 7/8 years. He is also a resident of a different village Daudpur half a mile away from the suit land. He has also no land near the suit land. It is clear that according to him plaintiffs has been possessing the suit land for 57 years which is contrary to the plaint case. Thus, PWs 2 and 3 are nothing but over zealous witnesses. It is difficult to rely upon the evidence of PWs. 2 and 3 regarding plaintiffs claim and possessions of the suit land. We have already noticed that PW 4 is a relation of plaintiff No. 11 and PW 5 is a man from a different village 3 miles off from the suit land and from his cross-examination it is clear that he is quite ignorant about the possession of PW Mobarak Ali or other plaintiffs. Court below, therefore, did not rightly rely upon the evidence of PWs 4 and 5. Except PW1 none of the other PWs. said anything about reclamation of the suit land by the plaintiffs. In the absence of any evidence to corroborate the PW 1 as to reclamation of the suit land by the plaintiffs statement of the PW 1 who is interested in the result of the suit in this respect cannot be relied upon. There is no averment or evidence on the side of the plaintiffs when they denied the title of the said landlords in the suit land and began to possess the same adversely to them.

<u>15. From the above discussion, it is clear that the plaintiffs' failed to prove their possession in the suit land Plaintiffs claim that they made the suit land fit for cultivation 40 years ago after taking settlement and grew paddy therein is also belied by the entry in the khatians Ext. A series classifying the suit lands as Layak patit layck/ura i.e. follow land in Khas possession of the predecessor of the proforma defendants. It is well settled that possession follows title. Even occasional surreptitious acts of possession on the part of the plaintiffs behind the back of such recorded owners who were admittedly residents of a distant place in the absence of any evidence of forcible entry in the land in denial of title of such owners cannot amount to adverse possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land.</u>

16. Court below did not assign any reason for finding the khatians Ext. A series to be erroneous and kabala Ext. C to have no legal effect, admittedly Syedunnessa Chowdhurani and others were the owners of the suit land and proforma defendants 14 to 21 as their heirs inherited the same. As the plaintiffs failed to establish their settlement of the same from the said landlords we find no reason how the court below could hold the said khatians in the names of the said landlords to be erroneous and the kabala in favour of the principal defendants to have no legal effect. Had the plaintiffs acquired any title in the suit land they would have paid rent for the same to the Government from 1363 BS after the acquisition of rent receiving interest. They utterly failed to make out any such case of payment of rent to the Government. How could the plaintiffs enjoy the suit land from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit as claimed by them without paying rent to the Government? Any lay cultivator is quite conscious that he cannot enjoy the land without paying rent to the Government. Had the plaintiffs acquired any interest or title in the suit land they would have endeavored to pay rent to the Government and would have taken steps at the earliest opportunity to get the Khatians corrected in their names. But they have been sitting idle and now have arisen from their deep slumber after lapse of such a long time when the principal defendants purchased the suit land from the proforma defendants. On the other hand, we find from Ext. B series that the contesting defendants paid rents for the years 1379-82 BS vide Ext. B series. These go to show that all previous rents were paid by the recorded owners of the said land as stated by the DW 1 in cross-examination.

<u>17. It is true that in the kabala Ext. C the suit land has been described as Halichara i.e. seedling bed. As the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land merely because the suit land has been described in defendants kabala as Halichara land will not lead to the necessary inference, that the plaintiffs had been or are in possession of the said land. Moreover it is not the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land is Halichara rather their case is that the suit land is paddy land which they failed to prove.</u>

18. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case of settlement of the suit land in their favour 40 years before the filing of the suit or that they acquired title in suit land on the basis of adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. As the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land their simple suit for declaration of title is barred under the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for want of prayer for further relief. The suit as framed is not also maintainable.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree appealed from is set aside and the plaintiffs suit is dismissed. In the facts and circumstances of the case parties shall bear their respective cost all through.

End.
